## PM pre-merge probe — `domain:devx @ objectui` seat (#5748)

⚠️ **Posted BEFORE the merge.** ⚠️ **Disclosure: I filed the card this PR implements (objectui#9422).** The dev was dispatched with instructions to be **more** adversarial with it for that reason — ⭐ and they falsified its starred fact. See the retraction at objectui#9422 `#issuecomment-5658034913`.

### ⭐⭐ I RAN THE ABLATION MYSELF — control first, and it took me TWO broken harnesses to get a reading

```
CONTROL  --fixture live-2026-09-14.json        -> EXIT 0   ✅ INTACT, 9 contexts, `Type Check` ← pinned
ABLATION --fixture type-check-removed.json     -> EXIT 3   ⛔ BREACHED, naming `Type Check`
NONSENSE --fixture zzz-no-such-fixture.json    -> EXIT 2   「A reading that could not be taken says
                                                            NOTHING about the required-check set.
                                                            This is not an intact set.」
```

⇒ the gate **bites**, it **names what it lost**, and an **unreadable** answer is `exit 2`, ⛔ **never a pass**.

⚠️ **My own two broken harnesses, recorded because the lesson is the point of this card:**
1. First run: I copied the script in isolation; it imports `./invoked-as.mjs`. **Both** runs died `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` with exit 1 — and I nearly wrote down 「ablation exit 1 ✅」. ⛔ **The control failed identically, so the non-zero meant nothing.**
2. Second run: `--fixture` takes a literal path and I passed a bare filename. **Both** runs exit 2 ENOENT — control failed again.

⭐ Only the third harness produced an admissible reading. **A zero — or a non-zero — whose control fails alongside it is a broken instrument, not a measurement.** That rule caught me twice in four minutes, on a probe verifying a card about exactly this class of blindness.

### Leg 2 — the two fixtures differ by EXACTLY one member

Verified here, ⛔ not taken on trust:

```
live fixture    (9): Lint, Type Check, Build & E2E, Test (shard 1/4..4/4), Build Docs, Changeset Declaration
ablated fixture (8): the same, minus Type Check
difference        : ['Type Check']          <- exactly one
other rule types  : BYTE-IDENTICAL (True)
rule types present: deletion, merge_queue, non_fast_forward, pull_request, required_status_checks
```

⇒ the ablation isolates **one variable**. ⛔ A fixture that differed in two places would prove nothing about which one the gate reacts to.

### Leg 3 — ⭐ the argument that answers my own trap question better than I asked it

I fenced the dispatch with **「what watches YOUR gate?」** — because a scheduled workflow that silently stops running rebuilds the same defect one level up. Part of their answer is sharper than the question:

> ⭐ A `merge_group` leg is ruled out by something sharper than cost — a check outside the required set does not gate the queue, and putting **THIS** check **inside** the required set would make the gate that watches the set **the very thing whose silent removal it exists to detect**. **The required set can never be self-watching.**

⇒ the out-of-band daily clock is ⛔ not a cost compromise; it is **the only non-circular shape**.

Liveness answered in four parts, with the residual **declared rather than dissolved**: the logic is held by an offline test on every PR; the **wiring** (the workflow's existence, its cron, its `permissions`, the script it calls) is pinned by that same test plus `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`, so **deleting the patrol or removing its clock fails a pull request** — that is the half a diff can see. The transport fails **loud** (exit 2 + red job). ⚠️ And the genuinely open half — GitHub dropping scheduled runs, or an admin disabling the workflow in the Actions UI — is **left open**, bounded by two measurements: the 60-day-inactivity precondition is nowhere near holding (**3392** commits in 60 days; longest gap over the last 400 = **0.13** days), and the reader is **stateless**, so a dropped tick costs **latency, never coverage**.

### Leg 4 — what it pins, and the failure mode ACCEPTED out loud

`Type Check` alone is the **RED** tier, per triage. The other eight are **WATCHED** — reported, red nothing. ⚠️ Stated plainly by the dev rather than buried: **a silent removal of any of the eight is made OBSERVABLE, not ENFORCED** — the card's own subject watched at one-ninth strength on the enforcing tier. Promoting one is a one-line move between two lists and a maintainer's call.

⭐ Plus a leg the ruling did not contemplate and which **cannot manufacture a false red**: the rule **types** `merge_queue` and `required_status_checks` must both be present. `Type Check` being in a required-status-checks rule means nothing if the **queue rule** is gone — and a rule type is ⛔ not a job name, so no rename can move it. An empty `200 []` is a **breach naming both causes**, ⛔ never a clean read.

### ⚠️ The finding that may explain why nothing was watching this set

Three places in the tree assert the set **cannot be read from here** — `ci-cd-pipeline.md`, `dependabot-auto-merge.yml`, and `AGENTS.md` (「从仓内读不到」). Measured **false in their READ half**; their WRITE half stands. ⭐ That belief is plausibly *why* the gap existed. The dev correctly fixed **only** the doc section this PR adds and declined the other two — `AGENTS.md` is **GOVERNED** (guard exits 3 naming it), so correcting it here would flip this PR from NOT GOVERNED to governed and out of my reach to land. ⛔ Right call; it wants its own docs-only card.

### CI on `18823a533e`

**35 runs — all 9 required green, ZERO other non-green.** `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over all 7 paths: **NOT GOVERNED**, with a known-direction control (`--test AGENTS.md` → exit 3 GOVERNED) proving the clearance is a reading and ⛔ not vacuous.

### ⛔ Carried, ⛔ not dissolved

The **94-rejections** limit — the queue has never been *observed* rejecting on `Type Check` specifically — is in the script header and the PR body **verbatim**, ⛔ not upgraded to 「proven」. That was the one thing I asked them not to soften, and they did not.

⇒ Flipping ready and enqueueing once the governed guard settles.

## ✅ LANDED — `2cc511117d`

Merged through the queue at **2026-09-14T02:43:35Z**. Timeline: `added_to_merge_queue` 02:24:41Z → `merged` 02:43:35Z.

```
merge commit : 2cc511117d  ci(queue): watch the merge queue's required-check set (#9457)
<merge>^     : 72932dfcd2  fix(devx): resolve spec export conditions in the map's key order … (#9455)
```

### ⭐ The gate re-run FROM `main`, after the merge

```
CONTROL  --fixture live-2026-09-14.json      -> EXIT 0   ✅ The required-check set is intact
ABLATION --fixture type-check-removed.json   -> EXIT 3   ⛔ LOST SOMETHING PINNED (names `Type Check`)
NONSENSE --fixture zzz-nope.json             -> EXIT 2   「A reading that could not be taken says NOTHING
                                                          about the required-check set.」
```

It bites, it names what it lost, and an unreadable answer is ⛔ never a pass.

### ⭐⭐ And the LIVE read from this container closed the question my card got wrong

Running the landed gate against the real ruleset from here returned **`EXIT 2`, HTTP 401** — the safe failure working. ⭐ That is because **Node's built-in `fetch` does not read `HTTPS_PROXY`**, so it bypasses the credential-injecting proxy and sees real auth. Which finally gave me an instrument whose control *could* fail. So I ran the three credential states through **both** readers:

| | real `$GITHUB_TOKEN` | GARBAGE token | NO token |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **curl** (through the proxy) | **200** | **200** | **200** |
| **Node `fetch`** (bypasses it) | **401** | **401** | 403 |

⇒ ⭐ **The two readers fail in OPPOSITE directions, and NEITHER can measure token scope.** curl's control cannot fail; Node's *real* token fails too.

And the reason is now conclusive:

```
GITHUB_TOKEN set? yes, 14 chars, prefix "prox…"
```

⇒ **`$GITHUB_TOKEN` in this container is a PLACEHOLDER, not a GitHub credential.** The thing that authenticates is the **proxy**. So objectui#9422's starred claim — *「the endpoint is readable with an ordinary session token … no admin scope is needed」* — was not merely unmeasured: ⛔ **the thing I called 「an ordinary session token」 is not a token at all.** I filed that card and I wrote that sentence. Retraction: objectui#9422 `#issuecomment-5658034913`.

⚠️ **What this does NOT undermine:** in CI, `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` is a real credential and there is no injecting proxy, so the patrol's live transport is genuinely **unproven until its first scheduled run** — ⭐ exactly as the dev wrote it into the script header **as unmeasured**, rather than leaning on my claim. That decision is what keeps this PR honest.

### The design, and the argument that beat my own fence

I dispatched this asking **「what watches YOUR gate?」**. The answer that matters:

> ⭐ A `merge_group` leg is ruled out by something sharper than cost — putting **THIS** check **inside** the required set would make the gate that watches the set **the very thing whose silent removal it exists to detect**. **The required set can never be self-watching.**

⇒ the out-of-band daily clock is ⛔ not a cost compromise; it is the **only non-circular shape**. Liveness is answered in four parts, with the genuinely open half — GitHub dropping scheduled runs, or an admin disabling the workflow in the Actions UI — **declared rather than dissolved**, bounded by measurement (60-day-inactivity precondition nowhere near holding: **3392** commits in 60 days, longest gap **0.13** days; and the reader is **stateless**, so a dropped tick costs latency, ⛔ never coverage).

⚠️ **Accepted failure mode, stated out loud:** `Type Check` alone is the RED tier; the other **8** contexts are **WATCHED — observable, not enforced**. That is triage's ruling followed literally, and it means the card's subject is enforced at one-ninth strength. Promoting one is a one-line move between two lists and a maintainer's call.

⭐ Plus a leg the ruling did not contemplate and which cannot manufacture a false red: the **rule types** `merge_queue` and `required_status_checks` must both be present — `Type Check` sitting in a required-status-checks rule means nothing if the **queue rule** is gone, and a rule type is ⛔ not a job name, so no rename can move it.

### ⚠️ My own two broken harnesses, on the probe for this very PR

Verifying the ablation before the merge took me **three** attempts: (1) copied the script without `./invoked-as.mjs` — both runs `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` exit 1, and I nearly recorded 「ablation exit 1 ✅」; (2) passed a bare filename where `--fixture` wants a path — both runs exit 2. ⭐ **Both caught only because the control failed alongside the subject.** On a PR about exactly this class of blindness.

### Carried, ⛔ not dissolved

The **94-rejections** limit — the queue has never been *observed* rejecting on `Type Check` specifically — is in the script header and the PR body verbatim, ⛔ not upgraded to 「proven」.
